225	// series refs. Compaction callers only request AllPostings, which is served from the
226	// precomputed ref list without re-reading the Head. Other IndexReader methods delegate to
227	// the caller-supplied filter, which encodes the compaction flow's notion of "matching series".
228	type headSelectedSeriesIndexReader struct {
229		*headIndexReader
230		selectedSeriesRefs seriesRefs
231	}
232	
233	type allSelectedSeriesPostings struct{ index.Postings }
234	
235	func (h *headSelectedSeriesIndexReader) Postings(ctx context.Context, name string, values ...string) (index.Postings, error) {
236		if len(h.selectedSeriesRefs.sortedByRef) == 0 {
237			return index.EmptyPostings(), nil
238		}
239	
240		selectedSeriesPostings := index.NewListPostings(h.selectedSeriesRefs.sortedByRef)
241		// This method is only expected to be called during compaction from the AllSortedPostings, with AllPostingsKey.
242		// The result of this method will be passed to SortedPostings().
243		// In order to avoid sorting head twice, but still return the correct results, we return a postings type with a marker here.
244		// This marker will be used by SortedPostings to swap the full postings by the ones sorted by labels.
245		// However, the results is still valid to be used as normal postings as well.
246		if k, v := index.AllPostingsKey(); name == k && len(values) == 1 && values[0] == v {
247			return allSelectedSeriesPostings{selectedSeriesPostings}, nil
248		}
249	
250		// This is not expected to be used, as headSelectedSeriesIndexReader is only expected to be used during compaction.
251		return index.Intersect(selectedSeriesPostings, h.head.postings.Postings(ctx, name, values...)), nil
252	}
253	
254	func (h *headSelectedSeriesIndexReader) PostingsForLabelMatching(ctx context.Context, name string, match func(string) bool) index.Postings {
255		// This is not expected to be used, as headSelectedSeriesIndexReader is only expected to be used during compaction.
256		return index.Intersect(
257			index.NewListPostings(h.selectedSeriesRefs.sortedByRef),
258			h.head.postings.PostingsForLabelMatching(ctx, name, match),
259		)
260	}
261	
262	func (h *headSelectedSeriesIndexReader) PostingsForAllLabelValues(ctx context.Context, name string) index.Postings {
263		// This is not expected to be used, as headSelectedSeriesIndexReader is only expected to be used during compaction.
264		return index.Intersect(
265			index.NewListPostings(h.selectedSeriesRefs.sortedByRef),
266			h.head.postings.PostingsForAllLabelValues(ctx, name),
267		)
268	}

units.headline: New benchmark helper builds head with N series of in-order samples
units.summary: Test-only helper that opens a DB with compactions disabled and appends totalSeries series in batches of 10k. It cannot affect production; it only feeds the benchmarks.
units.reason: Test-only helper in a _test.go file; no production effect.

units.headline: Benchmark CompactSelectedSeries across selected-fraction sizes
units.summary: New benchmark that rebuilds the DB on each iteration, with the timer stopped, and measures CompactSelectedSeries for selection fractions from 100% down to 0.1%. Test-only. The comment's claim that evicted series cannot be reused holds, which is why the DB is rebuilt every iteration.
units.reason: New benchmark only; cannot change production behavior.

units.headline: New public API compacts arbitrary series refs into blocks and evicts them
units.summary: New exported DB method. It holds cmtx, drops refs whose series have OOO data, writes one block per chunk range through compactHeadViewLocked, and then evicts the series from the head using an append-ID watermark guard. Selected series are removed even if they are not stale, so callers decide what data leaves the head.
focus: With isolation disabled, the append-ID guard does nothing, so samples appended concurrently during compaction can be lost (the LateAppend test confirms this).
Duplicate or unsorted refs from callers: the result keeps input order and duplicates; check the block writer accepts them.
The failure metric relies on the named return err; confirm every error path returns through it.
The 'num_skipped_ooo' log field also counts refs not found in the head.

issues.title: num_skipped_ooo log counts missing refs, not just OOO series
issues.failure_scenario: Passing 10 refs where 5 were already garbage-collected and none have OOO data logs num_skipped_ooo=5, which wrongly points operators to OOO data.

issues.title: Duplicate input refs are not deduplicated before block write
issues.failure_scenario: A caller passes [r, r]. sortedByLabels then holds the same series twice, and the index writer may reject equal consecutive label sets, failing the compaction.

units.reason: New public API that persists blocks and evicts head data; it affects data retention and concurrency safety.

units.headline: Test that CompactSelectedSeries evicts selected non-stale series with hint
units.summary: New happy-path test that checks eviction, the block hint, an unchanged HeadMinTime and the metrics. Test-only addition.
units.reason: New test only; no production effect.

units.headline: Test that nil or empty refs are a no-op
units.summary: New test asserting that empty input writes no blocks and does not bump the triggered counter. Test-only.
units.reason: New test only; no production effect.

units.summary: New test where one series spans two chunk ranges; it expects two hinted blocks and the series evicted. Test-only.
units.reason: New test only; no production effect.
